playbook.role: Spend Strip Mine where the exchange changes the game: on a unique utility land, a fragile color source, or the land that prevents the opponent from casting the next spell. Recursion turns one-for-one denial into an engine.

claims.summary: Strip Mine made lands answerable at almost no deck-building cost and showed that mana development itself could be attacked as a primary strategy.
Jason Carl’s December 3, 1997 DCI announcement adds Strip Mine to the Classic Type I restricted list effective January 1, 1998.
Contemporary July 2004 rules advice confirms that Crucible does not grant additional land plays.
Strip Mine can target a basic Forest. The speaker being on the play leaves the turn-one Elf unable to tap during speaker turn two; tapping and sacrificing the Mine is the activation cost.
